stale_state_hypotheses.description: A state variable that appears to track a checkpoint or baseline may remain stale after a later state mutation and then be consumed by another function.
stale_state_hypotheses.risk: historical reference is reused as if it were current state
stale_state_hypotheses.title: baseline may not represent current state

stale_state_hypotheses.description: A checkpoint value can be written in one transition and then read later as if it were a fresh epoch marker even though the underlying totals changed in between.
stale_state_hypotheses.risk: later settlement or accounting consumes historical state instead of the newest value
stale_state_hypotheses.title: checkpoint may preserve older state

stale_state_hypotheses.description: The accounting path may compute a delta from an older snapshot, causing previously-accounted growth to be counted again after another valid state-changing sequence.
stale_state_hypotheses.risk: state transition and settlement are incorrectly coupled to stale history
stale_state_hypotheses.title: settlement may reuse stale snapshot information

state_accounting_invariants: lastSnapshot, round must represent the intended current state rather than a stale historical reference
a baseline should correspond to the intended epoch or round
already-accounted growth should not be counted again in a later settlement or reward path
settlement should consume the correct state snapshot for the active sequence
repeated valid sequences should not retroactively change historical accounting
